text.title: llamaindex-sql-query Core Rules
text.summary: Rules for NL-to-SQL via LlamaIndex NLSQLTableQueryEngine: connection mode, table retrieval, schema constraints, SQL safety.

rule.statement: Always connect with a read-only DB user. NL-to-SQL must never have permission to DROP, DELETE, UPDATE, or INSERT.
rule.rationale: An LLM-generated DROP TABLE is one prompt away; the DB user is the only enforceable boundary.

rule.statement: For DBs with more than 20 tables, build an ObjectIndex of SQLTableSchema and retrieve top-3 relevant table schemas per query. Never dump the full schema into the prompt.
rule.rationale: Schema dumping on a 200-table DB consumed 8k tokens per query before the answer started.

rule.statement: For DBs with at most 20 tables, use the include_tables allowlist explicitly. Implicit selection over-includes.
rule.rationale: Allowlist forces the engine to surface only the schemas relevant to the workload.

rule.statement: Inject a LIMIT clause into every generated SELECT (default LIMIT 100 unless caller overrides).
rule.rationale: SELECT * with no LIMIT returned 10M rows in one incident, OOMing the worker.

rule.statement: Validate generated SQL columns against the actual table schema before execution; reject if any column does not exist.
rule.rationale: LLMs fabricate columns when uncertain; pre-flight validation catches it before the DB does.

rule.statement: Return both the generated SQL and the answer to the caller. Hide-the-SQL surfaces are not auditable.
rule.rationale: Showing the SQL is the user's only way to verify the model answered the right question.

rule.statement: Set a query timeout (5-15s) at the DB connection level. Unbounded queries from LLM-generated joins can run for hours.
rule.rationale: LLM-generated cross-joins on large tables can run to billions of rows; timeout is the only safe cap.

rule.statement: Forbid the engine from accessing tables containing PII unless pii_posture explicitly allows it.
rule.rationale: NL-to-SQL surfaces data through paraphrase; pseudonymisation in the prompt is not enough.

rule.statement: When table_count is above 20 AND schema_size_chars is large (wide tables whose DDL for even three retrieved tables would exceed the per-query token budget), the nlsql-spec MUST use SQLTableRetrieverQueryEngine over an ObjectIndex of SQLTableSchema with similarity_top_k at most 3 (r2), give every SQLTableSchema a one-to-two-sentence context_str so retrieval matches on table purpose rather than raw DDL, expose wide tables through read-only views or a column allowlist so each retrieved table's schema stays under a fixed character budget, and set sample_rows_in_table_info to 0 or at most 3. PII tables are excluded from the ObjectIndex, not merely from include_tables (r8). The spec MUST record the measured prompt token count per query (fm-02) and the read-only DSN, LIMIT injection, column validation and timeout from r1, r4, r5 and r7.
rule.rationale: Table retrieval bounds how many tables the LLM sees, not how wide they are: three 200-column tables re-create the 8k-token prompt that the ObjectIndex was supposed to remove (fm-02). Views and context_str are the two levers that shrink each table's footprint, and excluding PII at the index level is the only exclusion that survives a retriever that picks tables by similarity.

rule.statement: When table_count is above 20 AND schema_size_chars is ordinary, the nlsql-spec MUST use SQLTableRetrieverQueryEngine with an ObjectIndex of SQLTableSchema and similarity_top_k=3 (r2), a context_str per table, and NLSQLTableQueryEngine with the full schema is forbidden. The rest of the wiring is unconditional: read-only DB user (r1), LIMIT 100 injected into every SELECT (r4), generated columns validated against SQLDatabase.get_table_columns before execution (r5), SQL returned with the answer (r6), a 5-15 s connection-level timeout (r7) and PII tables excluded unless pii_posture allows (r8). The fm-02 detector result (tokens per query, expected 5-10x below a schema dump) is part of the record.
rule.rationale: Past 20 tables the prompt is dominated by schema the query never touches, so cost and hallucinated joins both scale with table count rather than question difficulty. Retrieving three relevant schemas per query is what keeps the prompt flat while the DB grows.

rule.statement: When table_count is 20 or fewer, the nlsql-spec MUST use NLSQLTableQueryEngine with an explicit include_tables allowlist naming only the tables the query surface needs (r3), with PII tables absent from that list unless pii_posture allows them (r8); an ObjectIndex / SQLTableRetrieverQueryEngine is NOT built on this branch. The unconditional wiring still applies: read-only DB user verified by the fm-01 DROP test (r1), LIMIT 100 injected (r4), column validation before execution (r5), SQL returned with the answer (r6) and a 5-15 s timeout (r7).
rule.rationale: With a small schema a retrieval layer adds an embedding index and a wrong-table failure mode without saving tokens worth measuring; an explicit allowlist is cheaper and auditable. The safety rules do not scale down with table count, because one write-capable DSN is one prompt away from fm-01 regardless of how many tables it can see.
